correctness.rationale: The zero-sum vectors on the n-shore form the m-eigenspace for 1≤m<n: the other shore contrasts have eigenvalue n and the two block-constant eigenvalues are 0 and N. The projector has rank n−1 and Frobenius norm √(n−1). In unitary Fourier convention UPU^T differs from M=UPU* by inversion of the column character, so neither entrywise absolute sum nor Frobenius norm changes. Translate B=A∖C to contain zero; this preserves the Fourier magnitudes and gives M1=0. In each row the off-diagonal entries sum to minus the nonnegative diagonal. Summing the triangle inequalities gives 2 tr M, with equality precisely when the off-diagonal entries are real nonpositive (a zero diagonal then requires the off-diagonal entries to vanish). In that case the quadratic form is a nonnegative weighted graph Laplacian. For every b∈B, Ue_b lies in the kernel. Each positive-weight edge must therefore join characters agreeing on B and thus on H=⟨B⟩. As an independent necessity check, for any h∈H the vector Ue_h is constant on all such edges, and hence is in the kernel of M. It follows that P e_h=0. For h∈C its squared norm would be 1−1/n>0; thus H⊂B and B=H. This also bypasses the frozen Parseval contradiction. For sufficiency, translate a subgroup coset to H. For nonidentity χ its sum over C is −m if χ is trivial on H and zero otherwise. The identity character row is zero. For distinct nonidentity χ,ψ in different restriction classes the diagonal-term Fourier coefficient at χψ⁻¹ vanishes and so does the product term. In the same class those entries have the form −(m+|S_C(χ)|²/n)/N, hence attain the rowwise bound. Lagrange and existence of every divisor subgroup order in a finite abelian group give attainment exactly for m|N, equivalent to m|n. The finite number of subsets then gives strict inequality otherwise, without claiming the nondivisible minimizers or value.
residual_risks: The balanced case combines two eigenspaces and is not covered by the spectral-projector identification. Finite enumeration and FFT tolerances are corroborative, not proofs of exact equality or of every group order.

originality.rationale: Exact primary-source comparison supports the factor-two bound and coset equality as a partial answer to the intermediate projector and labeling group questions, not a restatement of the rank bound, top projector result, or a result for the Fourier norm of a one-variable indicator. The global sharp value and all minimizers are determined in the divisible regime only. In the frozen relationship paragraph, the generic multiplicity statement is more precisely Ferguson et al.'s Lemma 7.1, citing the Gupta–Iosevich Theorem 7.2; Ferguson et al.'s own Theorem 7.2 gives the top result and strict intermediate bounds. This citation precision does not change the mathematical claim.

value.rationale: A sharp universal estimate and exact subgroup-coset rigidity determine the full set of optimizers in the natural divisibility regime, even outside cyclic groups. This is a structural partial answer to specified existing projector-labeling questions, not merely an improved numeric lower bound: attainment has a complete algebraic characterization.
residual_risks: The nondivisible minimum, opposite intermediate projector, and stability are not resolved by this result.
